system.description:
• Not every ranger works alone. Some build a partnership with the wild itself — starting with whatever creature will have them, and eventually earning the trust of things that shouldn't trust anyone.
  • Bonded Companion: Tame and bond with a beast companion that fights and travels alongside you.
  • At 1st level this is a mundane animal appropriate to the terrain (wolf, hawk, boar, etc.), bonded automatically over a few days of feeding and handling — HD equal to half your Ranger level (rounded up).
  • Your companion acts on its own initiative and will attack independently and automatically to defend itself or you whenever either of you is threatened — this costs you nothing.
  • Directing it to attack a specific target or carry out a specific action instead costs your own action.
  • This is the only Ranger kit that can bond with and permanently tame a beast companion this way.
  • At 6th level you may attempt to tame a beast-type monster of low power (giant spider, dire wolf, or similar, GM-approved) — this requires a sustained taming attempt (days of exposure and a Wisdom check set by the GM against the creature's HD and temperament) and can fail or provoke the creature into attacking.
  • At 10th level you may attempt the same against a genuinely dangerous beast-type monster (a young wyvern, a manticore, or similar apex predator, GM-approved) — the taming attempt is harder still, riskier to attempt, and failure is likely to mean a fight rather than a shrug. If a bonded companion is slain, a replacement of the appropriate tier can be found and a new taming attempt made after a season of searching.
  • Beastspeaker: Advantage on all checks to calm, communicate with, or avoid provoking wild animals and beast-type monsters, including ones far above what you could safely fight. This does not grant control over an unbonded creature — it only means the conversation has a chance.
